$comment: C66's /+3V3 escape via sat dead centre in its own pad -- the last via-in-pad
on this board that was not deliberate.
It had to be CLASSIFIED before it could be fixed, because three other
vias-in-pad here are correct and must stay: U4's five exposed-pad thermal
vias (the reason U46 windowed its paste), Q2's two plane stitches added by
U33, and U1.93's documented 0.5/0.2 exception. The test that settles it:
there is NO /+3V3 plane on Board3 -- the pours are /GND on Top, Bottom and
Inner1, and /+5V on Inner2 -- so a /+3V3 via cannot be stitching to a plane.
This one is a plain Top->Inner1 layer transition, the same reflow hazard just
removed from the four telltales and from C67.
Its siblings settle it too: C67 and C68 are the same 22 uF/0805 bulk cap on
the same rail at the other two panel connectors, and neither has a via in its
pad. C66 was the odd one out of three.
The Inner1 feed already runs north from the via, so north is the natural exit
-- and it is blocked: /VBUS_SENSE crosses on Top at -0.411. East is blocked
by /SCLK_L_MCU on Inner2 (-0.194). South is clear at 0.2239 to /+5V, so the
via goes south and the Inner1 feed runs the full length of the pad to meet
it. That costs nothing: the pad is top-only, so Inner1 passing beneath it
touches nothing. Feed clearance stays above 2.1 mm the whole way; the Top
stub clears by 0.44.

steps.step: 1/1  C66 -- via south out of the pad, Inner1 feed extended to meet it
$delete_note: Split in two on purpose. The Inner1 track runs from (47.600,97.500) to
(47.600,95.720), so deleting it needs a bbox reaching y=95.72 -- and a
single rule with vias:true then also swallows the SECOND via at that far
end, which is a different layer transition entirely. Doing that broke the
net (airwires 0 -> 1). So the track is deleted with vias:false over the
long span, and the via with a tight bbox around the pad end only.
